title: A Comparison of Retinyl Palmitate and Red Palm Oil β-Carotene as Strategies to Address Vitamin A Deficiency
authors: Souganidis E, Laillou A, Leyvraz M, Moench-Pfanner R
funder: This paper is part of fortification programs implemented worldwide by the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN) with the support of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and the Department for International Development (DFID).
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflict of interest. Two authors are employed by GAIN.
result: Narrative review. Carotenoids, particularly α- and β-carotene, are responsible for the orange-red colour of crude palm oil. Physical or chemical refining, both involving high-temperature deodorisation and deacidification under vacuum, removes some of the tocopherols and tocotrienols and destroys all carotenoids, yielding nearly colourless oil; a modified physical refining process patented by the Palm Oil Research Institute of Malaysia gives softly refined red palm oil that retains 80% of the original carotenoids. Only a fraction of β-carotene is retained when red palm oil is used for frying.
